newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Prague bourse, Central Europe index at year highs.
newsitem.headline: Prague bourse, Central Europe index at year highs.

text.p: Year records on Prague's bourse and a new year high in Budapest hoisted the Central European Share Index (CESI) to a 1996 high.
Elsewhere in the region Polish shares rose slightly, Bucharest gained vigour and Croatian stocks moved into positive territory. Slovak and Slovenian stocks eased.
PRAGUE
The Prague Stock Exchange posted year-highs despite listless trading. The PX50 index closed on Friday at 577.4, up 7.6 points, or 1.33 percent, on the week.
Komercni Banka and Ceska Sporitelna posted a late week rally to spur the bourse. But it was the performance of a few broader issues that continued to get most attention.
Rumours of takeover battles for beverage maker Seliko and glass fibre maker Vertex pushed prices through the roof.
WARSAW
Polish shares inched up after growth last week spurred by better July earnings reports. Analysts said there were few positive signals to break the market's current seesaw pattern.
But some analysts saw growth, with the market getting a boost next week from funds returned after the recent oversubscribed Kompap paper firm public offering.
The WIG index closed at 13,932 points, up 43.3 points or 0.3 percent from last Friday's close.
BUDAPEST
After three days of doldrums earlier in the week the market revived on Thursay and soared to a new high on Friday on what traders explained was fresh capital pumped into the market.
Recent privatisation and acquisition news had a beneficial impact, but market reaction to the release on Friday of first- half results from oil company MOL and packaging company Cofinec was mixed.
Led by the pharma sector several shares hit new high. MOL eased five forints to end at 1,550 and Cofinec ended at 5,300 forints, down 500.
On Friday the BUX index ended at 3,473.94 points, 116.85 points up on last Friday.
BRATISLAVA
Bratislava Stock Exchange shares drifted lower in another listless week of holiday trading, led down by blue chip losses.
The SAX index closed on Wednesday at 219.38, down 3.51 points, or 1.57 percent on the week, mainly on the back of a recent downtrend to shares of oil and gas storage firm Nafta.
BULGARIA
No corporate issues traded for a fourth week in a row on the Bulgarian stock market as investors preferred investments in foreign currency or treasury paper to company shares.
The lev has declined against the dollar throughout August, falling to a fresh low of 213 on the domestic interbank market on Thursday from around 187 early in the month.
Only the Sofia bourse operated with the Bulgarian Stock Exchange in recess until September 2.
The 13-share Reuter All Bulgaria Stock Exchange Index (RABSI) closed at 41.31 points, unchanged from last Thursday.
BUCHAREST
The Bucharest stock exchange gained vigour this week with overall turnover trebling to 217.8 million lei on Thursday and most prices picking up under strong demand.

The unofficial VAB Index -- a value-weighted index of all stocks computed by Vanguard SA securities -- was 2.9 percent higher from the previous session, closing at 384.3 points. It was 13.3 percent higher on the week.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks were mostly higher in livelier trade on Friday, closing on a firm note and market participants foresaw a week of steady expansion ahead.
Of the most active issues, drugs firm Pliva added 250 kuna to 11,500, 300 kuna higher than last Friday. Zagrebacka Banka ordinary shares were up five kuna closing this week slightly weaker at 675.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares eased 0.8 percent this week as the SBI index fell 7.67 points to 973.59. Total turnover was 256.8 million tolars ($1.9 million).
Financial consultancy Primofin was the leading decliner, falling 25.8 percent, while pharmaceutical trader Salus was the top gainer, rising 46.2 percent.
TIRANA

Albania's Savings Bank sold 400 million leks worth of a government bond maturing on August 1, 1998 to the Bank of Albania at Tirana's stock exchange's first weekly session on Monday. There were no transactions on Thursday.
